text.p: Italian bond futures ended lower in line with many other European bond markets and cautious ahead of a long weekend in Italy with markets here closed on Friday for Liberation Day, dealers said.

EMU worries continued to weigh on the market but traders noted that bond market reaction to Wednesday's European Commission and IMF reports indicating Italy may miss the single currency start had been less negative than could expected.
There was some disappointment that the Bank of Italy had not cut its discount rate after encouraging CPI preliminary data for April issued earlier this week, they added.
There was a generally cautious air in the market going into the long weekend with the G7 meeting ahead, so prices have tended to drift down throughout the afternoon, dealers added.
